blocks.body: Hydro jetting clears a sewer line with a high-pressure water stream, fed through the same cleanout access point used for rodding. A specialized nozzle sprays water in every direction as it moves through the pipe, scouring grease, scale, and roots off the entire pipe wall instead of just cutting a path through the middle. It's the fix for buildup that keeps coming back after rodding, or for roots that have worked into the pipe joints. Rodding opens the line back up. Hydro jetting cleans it.

img.alt: Diagram showing how hydro jetting clears a residential sewer line, with a cross-section view of the underground pipe, jet nozzle, high-pressure water spray, and debris being flushed toward the street connection

blocks.h2: Hydro Jetting Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: Is hydro jetting safe for a 100-year-old pipe?
items.preview: If it's intact, yes. We check first.
items.answer: If the pipe is still sound, yes. We camera it first and adjust the pressure. If a section is broken, a [repair](/geneva/sewer-repair) comes first.

items.q: Can jetting help a basement floor drain that keeps backing up?
items.preview: If buildup is the cause, yes. The camera tells us.
items.answer: If the floor drain line is coated with sediment, lint or grease, jetting clears it. If the camera shows roots or a break, we'll explain the repair options.

items.q: How is jetting different from rodding?
items.preview: Rodding opens a path. Jetting cleans the whole pipe.
items.answer: Rodding cuts through a clog. Jetting scours the entire pipe wall, removing grease, scale and roots instead of punching through them.

items.q: How long do the results last?
items.preview: Often years for grease and scale.
items.answer: For grease and scale, often years with good habits. Roots grow back over time.

items.q: How much does hydro jetting cost in Geneva?
items.preview: It depends on the line and buildup. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the length of the line, access and how much buildup there is. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
